dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a function φ : ℝ → ℝ, LocalDef001 φ means ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ φ: the universal real domain is convex and φ satisfies the defining convexity inequality there for all nonnegative real weights whose sum is 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is the left side of the asserted equivalence. Expanding it gives the standard two-weight definition of convexity of φ on all real numbers.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real-number instances selected in the target, it denotes ordinary real addition in t*x + (1-t)*y and t*φ(x) + (1-t)*φ(y).

dependency_coverage.name: Iff
dependency_coverage.meaning: Iff is logical equivalence between two propositions, requiring each proposition to imply the other.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target asserts equivalence, not merely one implication, between LocalDef001 φ and the displayed one-parameter inequality.

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Using the real order instance, it expresses 0 ≤ t, t ≤ 1, and the non-strict convexity inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard addition structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies ordinary real addition to the two sums in the displayed inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard less-than-or-equal relation on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the usual meanings of 0 ≤ t, t ≤ 1, and ≤ between the two real-valued sides of the inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard multiplication structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies ordinary real multiplication for weights times points and weights times function values.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instOne
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the distinguished multiplicative identity 1 in ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the upper endpoint of the weight interval and the constant in the complementary weight 1 - t.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is real subtraction, implemented as addition of the additive inverse.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.id
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a commutative semiring R, Algebra.id R is the canonical algebra structure of R over itself, with identity algebra map and scalar action induced by multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For R = ℝ, it supports interpreting scalar multiplication in ConvexOn as ordinary multiplication of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Algebra.toSMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: This operation extracts the scalar-multiplication structure carried by an algebra.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the ℝ-action on ℝ used by ConvexOn, so weighted points and weighted function values use the canonical real scalar action.

dependency_coverage.name: CommSemiring.toSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: This operation forgets commutativity from a commutative-semiring structure and retains its semiring structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides a semiring structure on ℝ where ConvexOn requires one.

dependency_coverage.name: ConvexOn
dependency_coverage.meaning: ConvexOn 𝕜 s f is the conjunction that s is convex over 𝕜 and that, for every x,y in s and every nonnegative scalars a,b with a+b=1, f(a•x+b•y) ≤ a•f(x)+b•f(y).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With 𝕜 = ℝ, s = Set.univ, and f = φ, it gives the precise left-side property: convexity of the whole real domain together with the two-weight Jensen inequality for φ.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the additive commutative-monoid structure on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the additive structure required by ConvexOn for both the real input space and real codomain.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instCommSemiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the commutative-semiring structure on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the canonical self-algebra and scalar action used in the definition of convexity.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.partialOrder
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the standard partial-order structure on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the order used for nonnegative weights and for comparing function values inside ConvexOn.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.semiring
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the semiring structure on ℝ.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the scalar semiring structure required by ConvexOn.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: Set.univ is the set containing every element of its ambient type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Here the domain of LocalDef001 is all of ℝ, so every real x and y satisfies the membership conditions in ConvexOn.

binders: φ is an arbitrary function from ℝ to ℝ.
On the right side of the equivalence, t is universally quantified over ℝ.
After the conditions on t, x and y are universally quantified over ℝ.
hypotheses: For the right-side inequality, t is assumed to satisfy 0 ≤ t.
Subject to that first assumption, t is also assumed to satisfy t ≤ 1; equivalently, t lies in the closed interval [0,1].
There are no restrictions on x or y beyond being real numbers, and there are no regularity assumptions on φ.
conclusions: For every φ : ℝ → ℝ, LocalDef001 φ holds if and only if, for every t in [0,1] and every x,y in ℝ, φ(t x + (1-t)y) ≤ t φ(x) + (1-t)φ(y).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 φ means ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ φ.
In this instance, ConvexOn means that the universal subset of ℝ is convex and that for every x,y in ℝ and every a,b in ℝ with a ≥ 0, b ≥ 0, and a+b=1, one has φ(a x+b y) ≤ a φ(x)+b φ(y).
The point t x + (1-t)y is the convex combination of x and y with complementary weights t and 1-t.
All additions, multiplications, subtractions, order comparisons, and constants are the standard real-number operations.
translation.proposition_plain_english: An arbitrary real-valued function on the real line is convex on all of ℝ in the supplied two-weight ConvexOn sense exactly when it satisfies the usual one-parameter convexity inequality: for every t between 0 and 1 and all real x and y, its value at t x + (1-t)y is at most t times its value at x plus (1-t) times its value at y.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is restricted to functions ℝ → ℝ on the entire real line; it does not state a version for general scalar fields, vector spaces, codomains, or proper convex subsets.
The right-side inequality is required only for t in the closed interval [0,1]. Because the bounds are represented by nested implications, values of t outside that interval impose no obligation.
The endpoint cases t=0 and t=1 are included, and the inequality is non-strict.

The left side syntactically includes the requirement that Set.univ be convex, in addition to the function inequality; for the canonical real structure this domain condition is automatically satisfied.
The proposition assumes no continuity, differentiability, measurability, strict convexity, or other regularity of φ.
Because φ has values in ℝ rather than an extended-real type, the statement does not encode infinite values or effective-domain issues.
The equivalence requires both directions; neither side is merely asserted as a sufficient condition.
